genesis.4.p1.b1.text: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain.

genesis.4.p1.b2.text: With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man

genesis.4.p1.b3.text: Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel.

genesis.4.p1.b4.text: Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the soil.

genesis.4.p2.b5.text: So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,

genesis.4.p2.b6.text: while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock.

genesis.4.p2.b7.text: And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but He had no regard for Cain and his offering.

genesis.4.p2.b8.text: So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.

genesis.4.p3.b9.text: Why are you angry, … and why has your countenance fallen?

genesis.4.p3.b10.text: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”

genesis.4.p3.b11.text: Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field,

genesis.4.p3.b12.text: Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.

genesis.4.p4.b14.text: I do not know! … Am I my brother’s keeper?

genesis.4.p4.b15.text: What have you done? … The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.

genesis.4.p4.b16.text: … Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, … When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.

genesis.4.p5.b17.text: My punishment is greater than I can bear. … whoever finds me will kill me.

genesis.4.p5.b18.text: If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.

genesis.4.p5.b19.text: So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

genesis.4.p6.b20.text: Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.

genesis.4.p6.b21.text: he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.

genesis.4.p6.b22.text: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.

genesis.4.p6.b23.text: And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron.

genesis.4.p6.b24.text: Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.

genesis.4.p6.b25.text: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”

genesis.4.p7.b26.text: God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.

genesis.4.p7.b27.text: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh.

genesis.4.p7.b28.text: At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
